description: Search every record by exact words and by meaning at once: meeting agendas and minutes, place dossiers, corridors, named patterns and briefs, entities and watch items. Finds a case, ordinance or resolution number, a parcel id or alternate key, an address, a project, firm or person, or a plain-language question. Ranking fuses three lists by reciprocal rank: full-text match (every word as written; "quotes", OR and -word work as in web search), title match, and voyage-4 embedding similarity. Each hit carries its true cosine `similarity` and `matched` (title, text, meaning). Every response states `scope` (the query names a covered place, a place outside coverage, or no place) and `evidence` (strong when a top record contains the query's terms or closely resembles it); when either needs explaining it adds a `note` and the coverage. `weak_match` is deprecated and will be removed in 2.4.0: it is true when scope is outside or evidence is not strong, so read those instead. Coverage: 25 jurisdictions in Lake, Orange, Osceola, Polk and Seminole counties, Florida, from 2024, listed in the coverage resource. Top 12.

q.description: A name, a number or a question. Text matching needs every word to appear in a record, so extra words narrow it; meaning matching tolerates any wording. Maximum 500 characters.

name: semantic_search

coverage.description: What the corpus covers; present with note. Same object as the coverage resource.

evidence.description: strong: a top record contains the query terms or closely resembles it (cosine >= 0.5). weak: records only loosely resemble it. none: nothing returned.

matched.description: Which rankings found the record: its title holds every query term, its text does, and/or it is among the 50 nearest by meaning.

similarity.description: True cosine between the query and the record embedding.

note.description: Present when scope is outside, evidence is weak, or nothing matched.

scope.description: Whether the query names a covered place, a place outside coverage, or no place.

weak_match.description: Deprecated since 2.3.0; removed in 2.4.0. True when scope is outside or evidence is not strong. Read scope and evidence instead.
